Lessons.Title: Comparing and Contrasting Data Distributions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: compare distributions with similar centers but different variability, rank their variability using dot plots, MAD and IQR, and explain why spread matters. Independent first-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 1 Lesson 11, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/1/11/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). Source roles: Building On HSS-ID.A.1, Addressing HSS-ID.A.2, Building Towards HSS-ID.A.3.

Original fictional task datasets in minutes: A=4,5,6,7,8 and B=0,3,6,9,12. Both have mean and median 6, but B is more dispersed. The exact values should be displayed on a common labelled number line, not independently stretched axes.

For A, absolute deviations from mean 6 are 2,1,0,1,2; MAD_A=6/5=1.2 minutes. For B they are 6,3,0,3,6; MAD_B=18/5=3.6 minutes. Using median-of-halves, A quartiles are 4.5 and 7.5 (IQR 3); B quartiles are 1.5 and 10.5 (IQR 9). This is a legitimate comparison because counts and units are the same.

Partner matching task: draw both dot plots and box plots, swap conclusions, identify the more variable group using independent numerical evidence, and decide how an occasional extreme would affect a measure of center. The source card-sort and group critiques are preserved as reasoning objectives; the first-party numbers are not publisher cards.

Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for accurate displays, correct two MADs, correct two IQRs and a comparative argument linking display shape and spread (maximum 8). Different correct graphs or explanations require human interpretation.

Source-activity A/B review, IM Algebra 1 First Edition U01:L11: Match source dot/box representations using consistent scales; rank spreads by MAD and IQR with shared center. Keep original first-party mathematical material and graphics; source artwork identity is NOT claimed. All physical/technology/partner work remains NOT_PERFORMED unless observed.

EDULYTIKS_AUTHORED_COOLDOWN (PUBLISHER_COOLDOWN_UNVERIFIED): Compare first-party groups with means 6, MAD 1.2 versus 3.6 and IQR 3 versus 9; explain which is more variable. A teacher scores 0, 1 or 2 per criterion: Correct MAD and deviations; Correct IQR/scale comparison; Variation interpretation. Total 6. No publisher protected Cool-down is claimed as read or reproduced.

KeyConcepts.Title: Variability
KeyConcepts.Definition: Spread describes how far observations differ from center and one another.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use a consistent measure for both data sets.
KeyConcepts.Example: A and B both center at 6 but MADs 1.2 versus 3.6.

KeyConcepts.Title: MAD comparisons
KeyConcepts.Definition: For equal units, higher MAD means greater average distance from mean.

KeyConcepts.Title: IQR comparisons
KeyConcepts.Definition: IQR measures the width of middle half of ordered data.
KeyConcepts.Rule: State the quartile convention and compare Q3-Q1.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare matching centers
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute means and medians of A=4,5,6,7,8 and B=0,3,6,9,12.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the given original data, show the computation and interpret the result in context.
Steps: Each set has five values and sums to 30.
Both sorted lists have middle third value 6.
Equal centers do not imply equal spread.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Both mean and median are 6 minutes for each group.
WorkedExamples.Check: Each sum 30 and each third value 6.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare MAD
WorkedExamples.Question: Which group has larger mean absolute deviation?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the given original data, show the computation and interpret the result in context.
WorkedExamples.Answer: B has three times A's MAD.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare IQR under median-of-halves
WorkedExamples.Question: Compute IQR for each of the two five-value sets.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the given original data, show the computation and interpret the result in context.
Steps: Exclude the middle value when finding quartiles.
For A lower pair 4,5 gives Q1=4.5 and upper pair 7,8 gives Q3=7.5.
For B lower pair 0,3 gives Q1=1.5; upper pair 9,12 gives Q3=10.5.
WorkedExamples.Answer: B has IQR 9, A has IQR 3 minutes.
WorkedExamples.Check: Both comparisons agree that B is more variable.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Equal medians reveal location, not variability.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compare IQR, MAD or display width.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Comparing graphs with different axis scales
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: An enlarged plot can exaggerate differences.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating the median-of-halves quartile convention as universal
CommonMistakes.Correction: State the convention in the solution.

SummaryPoints: Spread must be compared separately from the center.
Both original groups have mean and median 6 but B has higher MAD and IQR.
A: MAD 1.2, IQR 3; B: MAD 3.6, IQR 9 minutes.
Card matches and reasoned interpretations are teacher-scored.
